neighbours.label: word-internal pieces of prefixed biochemical terms (β-Al|anine, bi|opoly|mer, bio|cont|amin): a spelling unit
fire: Athletes often take beta-alanine before training to delay muscle fatigue.
The peptide chain begins with L-alanine and ends with a glycine residue.
Cellulose is the most abundant biopolymer on Earth and forms plant cell walls.
Researchers tested a biopolymer-based film as a wrapper for fresh cheese.
Hospitals screen ventilation ducts for biocontamination every six months.
The cleaning protocol removes biocontaminants from the surfaces of lab benches.
The label lists water, glycerin, beta-alanine and a mild fragrance.
Fungal spores are among the biocontaminants most often found in old libraries.
quiet: Athletes often take caffeine before training to delay muscle fatigue.
The peptide chain begins with a lysine residue and ends with a glycine residue.
Cellulose is the most abundant natural material on Earth and forms plant cell walls.
Researchers tested a starch-based film as a wrapper for fresh cheese.
Hospitals screen ventilation ducts for mould and dust every six months.
The cleaning protocol removes germs from the surfaces of lab benches.
The label lists water, glycerin, vitamin E and a mild fragrance.
Fungal spores are among the pollutants most often found in old libraries.

notes: Probe: beta-alanine 1.33 (peak 'anine'), biocontaminants 0.66 ('cont'), biopolymer 0.55 ('opoly'), bilby 0.37. Plain-word versions are 0.01. phenylalanine (split phen|yl|alan|ine) 0.009 and polypropylene 0.005. So the unit is tied to specific splits; fire items reuse the -al|anine, bi|opoly, bio|cont splits. Weak pole (max 10.75).
